subject: Follow-up: model behavior variants + proposed evaluation plan
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@optihealth.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: tom.reynolds@optihealth.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks + a few clarifying items from demo

Hi Dylan / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo today, and for walking through the latency / cost tradeoffs. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks to help OptiHealth prioritize the next evaluation steps: 

- What we care about most: minimizing hallucinations on long patient notes (1.5k–3k tokens), consistent instruction following for structured outputs (JSON tables), and predictable tail latency for batch inference (bursty daytime traffic).
- We heard you on caching and KV reuse; we want to validate that on our typical prefixes (~600 tokens).
- Competitive baseline: our infra team currently runs Bedrock (Anthropic + Claude) and Vertex Inference (Vertex AI) for a subset of features. We need a side-by-side focusing on hallucination rates and structured-output fidelity.

As next steps could you: 
1) Share a short test matrix and a handful of probe prompts we can run locally against our current endpoints?
2) Run a small A/B set on Redwood hosted vs Bedrock/Vertex for ~200 prompts (we can provide sample documents) and report hallucination rate + a short qualitative summary of failure modes?
3) Link to any runbooks or security checklist we should pre-share with our security team.

Attachments: demo-recording-20280716.mp4 (recording).

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Sr. Product Manager, OptiHealth
attachments: none in this message beyond the recording reference

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@optihealth.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks + a few clarifying items from demo

Hi Aisha — great questions and thanks for the clear priority list. Short recap + what we'll deliver by EOD Friday: 

Recap of priorities (from today):
- Hallucination rate on long clinical notes (1.5k–3k tokens)
- Structured-output fidelity for JSON tables and lists
- Tail latency under burst load + caching behavior for 600-token prefixes

What Redwood will provide:
1) A compact test matrix (attached as OptiHealth-Eval-Matrix.xlsx) with suggested probe prompts, acceptance criteria, and metric definitions (hallucination rate, rouge/factuality proxies, structured-output validity).
2) A small comparative run (we'll use a 200-prompt seed you can expand) that pits Redwood hosted (gptx-redwood-1 quantized baseline) against two hyperscaler endpoints (we'll emulate Bedrock/Vertex using our internal connectors where possible). We'll return per-prompt outcomes and a short failure-mode writeup.
3) Security/compliance starter pack and our SOC2 excerpt for your security team. If security needs anything else, please loop security@optihealth.ai and cc Laura Bennett from our compliance team.

Immediate asks for OptiHealth: 
- Send the 200 seed prompts (anonymized patient text is fine) or give us permission to use the prompt set in the attached matrix.
- Any strict success thresholds (e.g., <5% hallucination on structured fields) so we can prioritize tests.

Tentative timeline:
- Wed (24h): deliver matrix + prompt examples
- Thu–Fri: run 200-prompt comparison and return results + qualitative notes

I'll coordinate internally — looping Marissa for the eval plan and Ben for scheduling the dedicated run.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0142

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@optihealth.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model behavior variants + proposed evaluation plan

Thanks all — I built out the matrix Dylan referenced and attached the OptiHealth-Eval-Matrix.xlsx. High level notes and the probe set (summary):

Test axes (short):
- Context length sweep: prompts at 600, 1500, 2500 tokens to measure hallucination onset and KV cache reuse benefits.
- Instruction strictness: strict JSON-table instructions vs permissive natural-language outputs.
- Temperature / sampling variants: temp 0, 0.2, 0.5 to measure hallucination vs creativity tradeoffs.
- System prompt changes (safety vs factuality emphasis).

Proposed metrics and how we'll compute them:
- Hallucination rate: fraction of outputs containing fabricated facts relative to ground-truth annotations (binary per prompt).
- Structured-output validity: syntactic JSON validity + field-level correctness (automated check).
- Tail latency: 95th and 99th percentile on batch of 50 concurrent requests.
- Regression flags: any >10% drop vs baseline on structured-output validity triggers root-cause triage.

Probe prompt examples (we'll send full list in XLSX):
- "Extract structured medications and dosages from the following clinical note: <note>"
- "Convert the following encounter into the JSON schema: {patient_id, chief_complaint, diagnoses[], medications[]}"
- "Answer factual check: Is the statement 'Patient was started on metformin 500mg BID on 2024-05-02' supported by the note?"

Execution plan: 
- If OptiHealth supplies the 200-seed prompts we will run: Redwood-hosted quantized baseline + Redwood high-fidelity (non-quant) + two hyperscaler endpoints (as available).
- We'll produce a per-prompt CSV and a short 1-page summary of failure modes (hallucination types, instruction drift, truncation artifacts).

Attachments: OptiHealth-Eval-Matrix.xlsx (probe list + scoring rules).

Next steps for Aisha: please confirm we can pull the 200 prompts from your set or send the file; also confirm any redaction rules for PHI.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model behavior variants + proposed evaluation plan

Looping in Laura for compliance + scheduling. TL;DR — we can run the comparison on Thu (24th) morning in a dedicated slot; estimate ~3 hours of dedicated GPU time for the 200-prompt set across variants. Deliverables we'll hand back: per-prompt CSV, summary deck (2–3 slides), and annotated sample failures.

Operational asks: 
- Aisha: please confirm redaction rules (PHI allowed as tokenized placeholders or fully redacted?) and drop the 200 prompts in the Drive link Dylan shared (or send directly to me).
- Dylan/Marissa: I'll need a short list of exact endpoint variants to include (e.g., redwood-quant, redwood-fp16, bedrock-clf-v1, vertex-std). If you want us to include a long-context-configured variant (5120k kv window) say so and I'll add it to the run.

I'll carve out Thu 24th 09:00–12:00 PT as the run window unless someone objects. Once prompts + endpoints are confirmed I'll prepare the job and share a pre-run checklist.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1-650-555-0199
